integrated_description: The dog owner shall implement a formally bounded rain-play system consisting of: a physically fenced or pen-contained muddy play zone set well away from shared boundaries, supplemented by tarps or runners near boundary areas; mandatory active personal supervision during every rain session with a conditional pause triggered by heavy rain, heavily saturated ground, or any conditions where mud containment is likely to fail—substituting indoor enrichment alternatives during such pauses; and an immediate post-session paw-cleaning protocol with supplies staged and ready before the dog may approach any shared or boundary space. A written neighbor agreement must be executed specifying designated play zones, permitted play times communicated in advance, measurable cleanup standards, explicit owner financial responsibility for any damage that nonetheless occurs, and an enforceable escalation clause mandating temporary indoor restriction or stricter confinement if mud continues to reach the neighbor's garden despite the full protocol being in place.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders converged on the same five functional pillars—physical containment, active supervision, immediate cleanup, conditional no-play triggers, and a formalized written agreement with escalation—making full integration achievable without trade-offs. The only minor synthesis required was merging stakeholder_b's cost-responsibility clause and stakeholder_c's boundary-tarp measures into the shared physical-containment and written-agreement provisions, which strengthens rather than contradicts any single stakeholder's request.
